summary: Dedicated capacity: duplicate completions and unexpected billing spike during routing cache invalidation (Greenfield Health, EU-north)
description: Issue summary: Greenfield Health reported a large unexpected billing spike and multiple duplicated chat completions during a planned cache invalidation window on Dedicated capacity in eu-north. Impact: ~18k duplicate tokens billed to customer over a 35 minute window; several sessions observed duplicate message blocks (same content repeated twice or more) causing downstream dedup and audit failures. Compliance impact: customer runs PHI-bearing prompts; duplicates caused duplicate PHI entries in their logs which they flagged as compliance risk. Timeline: 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC — scheduled cache invalidation started; 02:08–02:43 UTC — elevated duplicated completions and billing; 02:46 UTC — mitigation (routing lockout) applied; 03:10 UTC — full rollback/patch deployed. This ticket tracks the incident, investigation, and post-incident actions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated capacity customer with prefix/KV caching enabled and an active routing policy that allows fallback to quantized variants. 2) Trigger a coordinated cache invalidation (prefix cache flush + KV refresh) across two routing pools within the same shard. 3) Generate concurrent streaming chat requests (concurrency ~120) pinned to the same session ids. 4) Observe duplicate completions returned to client and duplicate token accounting in billing logs. Observed behavior requires the exact interplay of cache flush and near-simultaneous routing re-evaluation; not reliably reproducible on single-node local setups.
logs_excerpt: 2026-03-10T02:08:47.421Z billing: token_charge request_id=abcd1234 tokens=432 charge=0.0012 note=duplicate-detected=false
investigation_notes: Initial customer report: 02:30 UTC - multiple sessions with back-to-back identical completions; customer noticed exact token-for-token duplicates.

Hypothesis 1: routing layer raced and sent the same request to two compatible pools (one with fresh cache, one with stale KV), both returned full completions which were merged/forwarded to the client as separate chunks.
Hypothesis 2: billing pipeline double-counted tokens when deduplication metadata was not attached to one of the worker responses during the invalidation window.

Checked routing traces: found 'dual-write' decision events during a transient state where pool health checks returned mixed states after the cache invalidate job kicked off (link to traces: https://grafana.redwood/traces/INC-20260310-01).
Checked worker logs: worker-83 and worker-127 both produced completion blobs for same request ids; t-server returned both blobs to the router before deduplication hook ran.

Billing audit: charging service received two independent token-charge events without 'dedup-id' header on the second, causing two separate charges (billing pipeline expects dedup token to suppress duplicates).
Repro attempt on staging: reproduced 3/5 runs when simulating coordinated cache invalidation across two routing pools and high concurrency; reproduced duplication and double-charges.
Security note: Greenfield's content included PHI; duplicates stored into their downstream EHR logs—escalated to Security & Compliance for retention guidance.

Related PRs: routing change added optimistic dual-write as a fast-fail protection during rollouts (PR referenced above) — that path did not properly set dedup headers when cache invalidation occurred.

Root cause (summary): A race between the cache invalidation job and a new optimistic dual-write routing code path resulted in two full completions being forwarded and billed. The deduplication metadata/headers were not consistently attached to the fallback response when the invalidation occurred mid-request.
Full postmortem scheduled on confluence page linked above.
resolution: Immediate mitigation (02:46 UTC): disabled optimistic dual-write routing for affected shard and applied a soft-lock to routing decisions while cache invalidation jobs are in progress.

Hotfix (03:10 UTC): patched router to attach dedup-id metadata to all fallback/dual responses and to enforce single-forward semantics if cache invalidation flag is present; deployed to eu-north via canary then rollout.
Billing remediation: issued credit for duplicated token charges to Greenfield Health covering the duplicate portion (~18k tokens). Finance and CS confirmed credit applied on 2026-03-11.

Customer communication: support call at 2026-03-10 11:00 UTC with account team, Security, and Engineering; shared mitigation steps and timeline; Greenfield requested follow-up evidence (logs and billing adjustment) which were provided.
Status: fix deployed and validated; no further duplicates observed in monitoring for 72 hours post-fix.
